p01.why: Members defined outside the class repeat the head in order, with the pack written as X..., so both checks hold and main returns 0.

p02.why: The defaults of the declarations add up from right to left, so Pair<> is Pair<char, int>.

p03.why: The two declarations of Box have heads with different numbers of parameters.

p04.why: Unnamed parameters, a trailing pack, and a template template parameter with class and typename are all valid.

p05.why: Each kind of parameter can have a default, and a default can name earlier parameters.

p06.why: A pack must be the last parameter of a variable template.

p07.why: Each specialization of a variable template is its own variable, so limit<long> keeps 10.

p08.why: A class with a private data member is not a structural type, so it cannot be the type of a constant parameter.

p09.why: An alias template specialization is the aliased type, and T is deduced through Pointer<T>.

p10.why: In the outside definitions the non-dependent base B and the member Size hide the parameters with those names, so the sizes are 16 and 8.

p11.why: The default ends at the first >, so 3 > 4 must be in parentheses.

p12.why: In an alias template each parameter after one with a default needs a default.

p13.why: A template template parameter pack must not have a default.

p14.why: In a variable template each parameter after one with a default needs a default.

p15.why: A member template defined outside a class template needs two heads, not one head with both parameters.

p16.why: The > is inside parentheses, so the default is false.

p17.why: The two declarations differ in the kind of the parameter.

p18.why: A constant parameter of array or function type is adjusted to a pointer type.

p19.why: TPL-42 makes it valid and Clang and EDG accept it, but GCC rejects the member enumeration defined after the class under -pedantic-errors (Q-0199).

p20.why: Class template packs are last, and in the function template the parameter after the pack is deduced from the call.

p21.why: The constant parameters have different types, int and long.

p22.why: TPL-18 says a friend function named after a parameter is valid and Clang and GCC accept it, but EDG rejects it when the class template is used (Q-0198).

p23.why: The alias template uses itself in its own type.

p24.why: One declaration has a pack and the other does not.

p25.why: The placeholder gets the type Secret, which has a private data member and so is not structural.

p26.why: Array and function parameter types become pointers.

p27.why: A constant pack in a member template can be typed by the type pack of the enclosing class template.

p28.why: Function templates and a plain function share the name, and the plain function wins for a double argument.

p29.why: The template template parameters have heads that are not equivalent.

p30.why: Two declarations both give a default for T.

p31.why: The parameter T hides the global struct T inside the template only.

p32.why: Each specialization has its own static member, so the addresses differ between Tag<int> and Tag<char>.

p33.why: The pack must appear as T... in the argument list of the outside definition.

p34.why: main must not be a template.

p35.why: A template template parameter can use class or typename.

p36.why: N is a prvalue, so its address cannot be taken.

p37.why: In an alias template a pack must be last.

p38.why: A template must not be declared at block scope.

p39.why: Class, function, variable, alias, and member templates all work as written.

p40.why: A class template definition must not be followed by a declarator.

p41.why: class and typename mean the same thing, and redeclarations can mix them.

p42.why: A class with a mutable member is not structural.

p43.why: In the second declaration T has a default but U has none in any declaration.

p44.why: Two declarations of fill both give a default for T, even though the defaults are the same.

p45.why: Counter<int> and Counter<char> have separate count members, and the static member variable template gives sizeof(short).

p46.why: A variable in the body must not reuse the name of a template parameter.

p47.why: Every parameter type is structural and every argument is a constant of that type.

p48.why: The call picks the plain function twice(int), which is declared but never defined, and the template does not define it.

p49.why: An int parameter is a prvalue, a reference parameter is an lvalue of int, and a class parameter is an lvalue of const Point.

p50.why: A variable template declaration must not have two declarators.

p51.why: Pointer<int> is int*, so the two take declarations declare one function.

p52.why: Back follows a pack, has no default, and is not deducible; Clang and GCC accept the declaration and EDG rejects it (Q-0195).

p53.why: The member defined outside uses its own head's default char, and the inside member uses int, so the sizes are 4 and 1.

p54.why: A pointer to void, with or without cv, is a structural type, and the arguments are constants.

p55.why: The heads of partial specializations can put a pack before another parameter (TSP-9).

p56.why: Top-level const is dropped, so the two heads match and N is a prvalue int.

p57.why: The argument list after Pair lists the parameters out of order.

p58.why: The placeholder would get the type void, which is not structural.

p59.why: A local class must not declare a member template.

p60.why: A member class can be defined after the class body with the class head.

p61.why: A non-static data member must not be a template.

p62.why: GCC and EDG give one closure type for two uses of Closure<int>, but Clang gives two, so Clang fails the static_assert (Q-0200).

p63.why: An rvalue reference is not a structural type.

p64.why: In a class template U follows a parameter with a default and has no default.

p65.why: Equal class arguments name one object in the whole program, also across the two templates, and different values name different objects.

p66.why: A template must not have C language linkage.

p67.why: The member function template is defined outside with two heads, and the member class template works.

p68.why: The class parameter is one static object for equal arguments, so the addresses compare equal in a constant expression.

p69.why: void is not a valid constant parameter type.

p70.why: The outside definition uses its own head, which has no inner default, so C<> lacks an argument.

p71.why: Redeclarations can use different parameter names when the heads are equivalent.

p72.why: A class template must not have the name of its own parameter.

p73.why: A friend declaration that is not a definition must not give a default template argument.

p74.why: An explicit specialization must not have C language linkage.

p75.why: A typedef declaration is not valid after a template head.

p76.why: The friend definition with a default must be the only declaration; Clang and GCC accept the second declaration and EDG rejects it (Q-0197).

p77.why: Valid by TPL-42 and accepted by Clang and EDG, but GCC rejects the enumeration defined after the class under -pedantic-errors (Q-0199).

p78.why: In a class template the pack T... is not last, and V is typed by a pack of the same head.

p79.why: Owner has a user-provided destructor, so it is not a literal type and not structural.

p80.why: A constant parameter must not have a storage class specifier.

p81.why: A variable template must not reuse the name of a class template in the same scope.

p82.why: A constant parameter pack must not have a default.

p83.why: A member template defined outside the class must not give a default in its own head.

p84.why: The member function and the static member are defined outside, and value starts at 7.

p85.why: A type parameter pack must not have a default.

p86.why: Each parameter after a pack is deduced or has a default, so all three calls work.

p87.why: A local class must not declare a friend template.

p88.why: The plain function wins without a template argument list, and twice<int> uses the template.

p89.why: The two templates differ in their heads, so each explicit argument picks one.

p90.why: A call without <> prefers the plain member, and a call with <> uses the template.

p91.why: Template template parameters can take a constant parameter head or a pack head.

p92.why: A class template must not share its name with a variable in the same scope.

p93.why: A member definition outside the class must not give a default in the class head.

p94.why: A class without a name is not valid after a template head.

p96.why: The parameter type Wrap is deduced from each argument as by class template argument deduction, giving Wrap<int> and Wrap<char>.

p97.why: Top-level volatile and const are dropped from constant parameter types.

p98.why: N is a prvalue and cannot be assigned.

p99.why: A partial specialization must not have C language linkage.

p100.why: Two specializations with different arguments give different closure types.

p101.why: A non-static data member must not be a template.

p104.why: The friend template definition with a default is the only declaration and is found by argument-dependent lookup.

p106.why: A plain class can hold member class, variable, alias, and function templates.

p107.why: Two parameters in one head must not have the same name.

p108.why: A member function template must not be virtual.

p109.why: auto takes the type of the argument, and decltype(auto) keeps the reference for (object).

p110.why: A function template can have defaults in any order because U is deduced.

p111.why: A constant parameter declaration must not define an enumeration.

p112.why: A namespace member B does not hide the parameter B, so sizeof gives 1.

p113.why: A destructor must not be a member template.

p114.why: Self<int> uses itself through a member of Holder<int>.
